answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand deposits. Like an atlas mapping every route, the registry tracks each identity's attested work over time; a velvet-smooth onboarding still hides no history, and an ivory-tower newcomer with no record earns slowly until its work is verified. Attackers pay full price per fake while honest agents amortize one stake across a long useful life.
